title: The Draft Isn't Free at a Million Tokens
hook: Speculative decoding assumes the draft is cheap. At million-token context the draft head reads the entire KV cache every step — and can end up slower than no speculation at all.
key_points: Built-in Multi-Token-Prediction draft heads typically run full attention over the whole KV cache at every draft step.
That read grows linearly with context and comes to dominate draft cost exactly where speculation should pay off most.
The effect compounds with draft length, and sharpens under hybrid or linear-attention targets whose verification is already cheap.
Windowed-MTP applies a StreamingLLM-style sliding window plus attention sink to the draft's attention only.
Lossless by construction: the full-attention target still verifies every accepted token, so windowing changes proposals, never acceptances.
At 1M context it drops ~99% of KV entries for the draft and cuts per-decode-step cost 28-44% across three architecture families.
content_html: Speculative decoding works by having a cheap draft propose tokens that the expensive target verifies in parallel. Frontier models increasingly ship a built-in Multi-Token-Prediction (MTP/NEXTN) head for exactly this, on the assumption that the draft costs almost nothing. This paper points out where that assumption breaks: at very long context.
extra_html:
The draft-KV tax

An MTP draft head typically attends over the entire KV cache at every draft step, so its read grows linearly with context length. At a million tokens that read dominates the draft's cost — precisely in the regime where speculation is most valuable. It compounds with draft length, to the point where a deep native draft can go net-negative and run slower than not speculating at all. It's worse under hybrid and linear-attention targets: their verification pass is cheap, which leaves the draft's full-attention read as the exposed bottleneck.

The fix, and why it's safe

Windowed-MTP applies a StreamingLLM-style sliding window plus attention sink to the draft's attention only, leaving full-attention verification untouched. It's training-free and drop-in, and it's lossless by construction: the target still decides every accepted token, so a worse-informed draft can cost acceptance rate but never correctness. Bounding the draft's KV working set to a constant drops roughly 99% of KV entries at 1M context. Measured on Qwen GDN-MoE (35B and 122B) and a Mamba2-hybrid NoPE 120B at 1M context on a single GPU in SGLang, it cuts per-decode-step cost over the shipping native draft by 28-44% — an input-invariant margin that widens with context — and the now-unread draft KV (7.7-11% of total at 1M) is reclaimed with a ring buffer. Valliappan, arXiv 2026.

related.title: Speculative Decoding
related.hook: Let a small, fast model guess the next few words, then have the big model check them all in one shot. Same output, fewer slow steps.

related.title: JetSpec: Breaking the Scaling Ceiling of Speculative Decoding
related.hook: Speculative decoding stalls when bigger draft trees stop paying off. JetSpec trains a causal parallel draft head that drafts in one pass yet stays branch-consistent — hitting up to 9.64x speedup.

related.title: The KV Cache & Continuous Batching
related.hook: Generating one token reuses every prior key and value - that growing cache is why LLM inference is memory-bound, and continuous batching is how servers fight back.

related.title: A Hobbyist CUDA Kernel Brings DeepSeek-V4 Flash's Full 1M Context to One GPU
related.hook: Missing CUDA support for DeepSeek-V4 Flash's sparse-attention indexer meant llama.cpp needed ~256GB of VRAM for 1M-token context. One contributor's kernel patch shrinks that to a single RTX 5090.

flashcards.prompt: Why does a built-in MTP draft head stop being cheap at million-token context?
flashcards.back_html: It runs full attention over the entire KV cache at every draft step, so its read grows linearly with context until it dominates the cost of drafting.

flashcards.prompt: Why is Windowed-MTP lossless despite the draft seeing only a sliding window?

choices.text: The full-attention target still verifies every token, so windowing changes which tokens are proposed, never which are accepted
The window is large enough that no relevant token is ever excluded
It re-runs the draft with full attention whenever confidence is low

flashcards.explanation_html: Speculative decoding's guarantee comes from verification. Degrading the proposer can only cost acceptance rate, never output correctness.

flashcards.prompt: Under what kind of target model does the draft's full-attention read hurt most?
flashcards.back_html: Hybrid or linear-attention targets — their verification is already cheap, so the draft's quadratic-style full-context read is left exposed as the bottleneck.
